verdict.rationale: Veo's docs say it turns text prompts and images into short videos and claim character consistency, so the core image-to-video capability is documented. Whether the subject and composition are preserved is only implied. One hands-on report says Whisk (running Veo 2) redraws the whole image so the video barely resembles the source; that weakens confidence, but it concerns the Whisk surface on an older model rather than a direct counter-example to Veo's own image-to-video. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of subject/composition fidelity to the source image, independent hands-on corroboration that image-to-video preserves the input, and detail on image-conditioning controls.
